correctness.rationale: PASS. On the 2m-cycle, m>=4, with antipodal chord weight κ, each equispaced ± unit twist is an equilibrium with negative chord conductance −κ and positive ring conductance cosδ. Fixed-endpoint two-arm Dirichlet energy is at least 2 cosδ (v_m−v_0)^2/m, giving exactly one additional zero mode at κc=2cosδ/m, and one unstable direction above it. For broken branch, arm increments δ±x with 0<x<δ, current balance reduces to 2cosδ sin x=κ sin(mx). The ratio κ(x) grows continuously from κc to infinity since cot x−m cot(mx)>0 for x∈(0,δ), so every κ>κc gives exactly one positive x. Sign reversal and arm interchange yield four distinct equilibria. Along either branch c±=cos(δ±x)>0, and the harmonic energy lower bound gives [(c++c−)/m−κ cos(mx)](v_m−v_0)^2; equilibrium converts the bracket to positive [2cosδ sin x/m][cot x−m cot(mx)]. Thus all four branch Hessians have precisely one rotational zero mode, every other eigenvalue positive (flow stable), while synchrony persists. The principal chord gap π−mx crosses π/2 at κo=2 cosδ sin(π/(2m)); the square-root onset follows κ/κc=1+(m²−1)x²/6+O(x^4). Own independent full vector-field and Hessian construction passed 108 branch states m=4..12. The theorem says at least five, not exactly all stable classes.

A single natural graph perturbation destroys canonical twisted equilibria at a sharp threshold but generates four explicitly stable symmetry-broken branches persisting for all stronger chord coupling.
